extracted.subtask_description: Local/national/international news copy for a newspaper (Cold War-era reporting covering congressional investigations, defense production, diplomatic restrictions, and human-interest items). Includes embargo/advance release notes and multiple short dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft inventory (flyable aircraft)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIRCRAFT INVENTORY WHEN “FLYABLE” AIRCRAFT SINCE THAT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the major items Johnson said his group's investigation will cover; committee investigators are seeking facts from military officials and the aircraft industry about inventories of flyable aircraft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft losses (enemy action and obsolescence)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIRCRAFT LOSSES THROUGH ENEMY ACTION AND THROUGH OBSOLESCENCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated by the committee as a distinct area of inquiry to determine causes of reductions in available airpower and to compare wartime attrition vs. aging/obsolescence effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft production compared to Soviet production
rubrics_metrics.description: AIRCRAFT PRODUCTION AS COMPARED TO SOVIET AIRCRAFT PRODUCT[ION]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee intends to compare U.S. aircraft production rates and output with Soviet production as part of assessing relative airpower; part of broader fact-finding on production capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity and quality of aircraft in production and production prospects
rubrics_metrics.description: QUANTITY AND QUALITY OF AIRCRAFT NOW IN PRODUCTION AND PROSPECTS FOR PRODUCTION AND FUTURE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation item covering both numerical output and performance/technological quality of aircraft currently being produced and expected future capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations of the current production program and steps to break bottlenecks
rubrics_metrics.description: OPERATIONS OF THE CURRENT [PRODUCTION PROGRAM] — [STEPS] BEEN TAKEN TO BREAK BOTTLENECKS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee will examine how the current production program is run and what measures have been taken (or not taken) to eliminate manufacturing bottlenecks that slow defense output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee duty to analyze President's annual message and recommend to Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: UNDER THE LAW THE COMMITTEE IS REQUIRED TO ANALYZE THE PRESIDENT'S ANNUAL MESSAGE AND MAKE ITS OWN RECOMMENDATIONS TO CONGRESS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a statutory/procedural obligation of the joint committee: review the President's economic message and produce an independent report and recommendations for Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Department appeal right for persons under investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: UNDER THE STATE DEPARTMENT REGULATIONS, A PERSON UNDER INVESTIGATION HAS THE RIGHT TO APPEAL THE BOARD'S FINDINGS TO THE SECRETARY OF STATE OR A PERSON DESIGNATED BY THE SECRETARY TO [HEAR THE APPEAL].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains procedural protections available to individuals under loyalty/security review (right to appeal board findings to the Secretary or a designee; example: Nathaniel Davis was designated to hear Clubb's appeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embassy personnel travel restriction around Moscow (25-mile limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBASSY PERSONNEL ARE RESTRICTED TO A TRAVEL AREA OF 25 MILES AROUND MOSCOW, AND EVEN WITHIN THIS AREA CERTAIN PLACES ARE FORBIDDEN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diplomatic/security travel regulation cited as a retaliatory restriction imposed in January; specifies both an outer limit and additional internal prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: News dispatch embargo / advance-for-use timing
rubrics_metrics.description: FOR USE AT 7 P.M. EASTERN STANDARD TIME TODAY / END ADVANCE FOR USE AT 7 P.M. EASTERN STANDARD TIME
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production/press-note instructing the timing for release of the advance copy; functions as an embargo/embargo-lift instruction for distribution and publication scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navy 'bone bank' preservation method (freeze-dry + airtight, room temp storage)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOTH THE BABY AND ADULT BONES ARE KEPT IN AIR‑TIGHT BOTTLES AT ROOM TEMPERATURE AFTER FIRST BEING SUBJECTED TO THE 'FREEZE‑DRY' TECHNIQUE DESIGNED TO ASSURE PRESERVATION WITH VIRTUALLY NO DETERIORATION DUE TO INTERNAL CHEMICAL CHANGE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical/procedural standard used by the Naval Medical School's bone bank for preserving graft material; includes rationale (prevents chemical deterioration) and storage conditions (airtight, room temp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal Military Training (UMT) legislative provision — training & reserve term
rubrics_metrics.description: THE UMT LEGISLATION PROVIDES THAT YOUTHS OF 18 AND OLDER BE GIVEN SIX MONTHS MILITARY TRAINING AND BE IN THE RESERVES FOR 7 1/2 YEARS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative requirement/specification for the proposed UMT program describing age eligibility, training duration, and subsequent reserve service term; cited in reporting on congressional consideration.
